> **Pipeline step 01 — TPS landscape catch models (supporting model set).**
>
> **Purpose.** Fit the 10 landscape-only TPS catch models (outflow and the two distance terms,
> no water quality) on the larger no-water-quality dataset, score with moment-matched PSIS-LOO,
> and write LOO sidecars + the ranking used by `05_figures/model_comparison_forest.Rmd`.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tow_12_6_tps_nona.csv`.
>
> **Outputs.** `fits_tps_landscape/fit_tps<N>.rds`, slim LOO sidecars `loo_tps<N>.rds`,
> `fits_tps_landscape/fit_tps_landscape1-10_catch_loo_comparisons.csv`.
>
> **Cost.** Several minutes per model; fitting chunk is `eval=FALSE`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Landscape (TPS) analogue of `02_edsm_catch_models/edsm_catch_kfold_models.Rmd`, but this analysis stays with
PSIS-LOO + moment matching rather than grouped K-fold CV: each row of `tow_12_6_tps_nona` is an
independent tow sample (there is no `(1|StationCode)` grouping here), so leave-one-observation-out
is the correct cross-validation unit.

The code is functionalised the same way as the EDSM/fork-length k-fold notebooks:
  * one `fit_defs` table describes every model (fit 1..10),
  * one runner fits the model, computes moment-matched LOO, saves the full fit AND a lightweight
    LOO sidecar, and appends the summary to the shared text file,
  * the ELPD comparison + stacking weights at the end read only the small LOO sidecars, so model
    comparison/plotting never reloads the multi-GB fits.

This is its OWN fit set on its OWN dataset (`tow_12_6_tps_nona`, no water-quality covariates),
written to its OWN directory. It is NOT comparable, ELPD-for-ELPD, with the EDSM `tps_wq` k-fold
set: those use a different dataset that was z-scored independently, so the scales differ. The only
reason the sampler settings and the predictor/dispersion priors (b, shape) are matched across the
three notebooks is methodological consistency — so any difference in inference reflects the data,
not how the models were fit. The intercept and smooth-SD priors are left at brms defaults because
they live on each dataset's own scale (see the Priors chunk).

Settings (iter = 3000 / warmup = 2000, max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99, negbinomial,
offset(log(Volume))) mirror the EDSM k-fold notebook. Unlike the k-fold notebooks,
`save_pars(all = TRUE)` is kept here because moment matching needs the auxiliary draws.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(loo)
library(DHARMa)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Config — single source of truth for paths.
New, dedicated directory: these landscape fits are a separate fit set on a separate dataset
(no WQ covariates) and must NOT be mixed with the EDSM `fits_tps_wq_Vfix` outputs.
```{r}
FIT_DIR <- "fits_tps_landscape"
OUT_TXT <- file.path(FIT_DIR, "tps_landscape_fits_output.txt")   # appended printout
if (!dir.exists(FIT_DIR)) dir.create(FIT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)
```

Load TPS landscape dataset (one independent tow per row).
```{r}
tow_12_6_tps_nona <- read_csv("data/tow_12_6_tps_nona.csv")
```


###################################
Priors.
Methodological consistency across the three notebooks means matching prior *informativeness*,
NOT literal numbers (the datasets are z-scored independently, so no direct ELPD comparison).
  * b       normal(0, 2.5) — on the common z-scored predictor scale, so IDENTICAL to EDSM is
                             correct. Tested estimates (-0.9..1.8) sit comfortably inside.
  * shape   gamma(2, 0.1)  — negbinomial dispersion; same scale, kept identical to EDSM.
  * Intercept + sds        — LEFT AT brms DEFAULTS (student_t(3, -10.3, 2.5) and
                             student_t(3, 0, 2.5)). These parameters live on THIS dataset's own
                             scale: EDSM's normal(-5.5, 2) intercept sits ~3.4 SD from this
                             dataset's posterior (~-12), and normal(20, 5) on sds would inflate
                             the smooth (data supports sds ~1-5, model-dependent). The defaults
                             are weakly informative and auto-scaled, so they keep the same "let
                             the data speak" stance as the k-fold notebooks without mis-centering.
Diagnostics on the null model and the most-complex model both showed 0 divergences, 0 treedepth
saturation, E-BFMI ~0.9-1.1, max Rhat <= 1.005 -> clean posterior exploration.
########################################
```{r}
catch_priors <- c(prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "b"),
                  prior(gamma(2, 0.1),  class = "shape"))
```


###################################
LOO helper.
Computes PSIS-LOO with `save_psis = TRUE`, then moment-matches it (loo_moment_match needs the
full posterior, hence save_pars(all = TRUE) on the fit) and stores it on the fit under
`fit$criteria$loo`, exactly as the original notebook did.
########################################
```{r}
add_loo_mm <- function(fit, moment_match = TRUE, cores = parallel::detectCores()) {
  loo_result <- loo(fit, save_psis = TRUE, cores = cores)
  if (moment_match) {
    loo_result <- loo_moment_match(fit, loo = loo_result, cores = cores)
  }
  fit$criteria$loo <- loo_result
  fit
}

# Slim a loo object down to what loo_compare() / loo_model_weights() actually use
# (estimates + pointwise). The psis_object holds the full 4000 x N log-lik/weights matrix
# (~27 MB) and is NOT needed for ranking or stacking. Dropping it turns the "lightweight"
# sidecar from ~25 MB into ~60 KB, which matters here because large .rds files in this
# iCloud-synced folder get evicted and then fail to read mid-batch ("error reading from
# connection"). The full loo (with psis_object) still lives inside the big fit's $criteria$loo.
slim_loo <- function(loo_obj) {
  loo_obj$psis_object <- NULL
  loo_obj
}

# Robust readRDS for this iCloud-synced folder. If a file has been evicted to the cloud, the
# first read can fail ("error reading from connection"); we force macOS to materialize it
# (brctl download, then fault the bytes in with a full read) and retry a few times.
read_rds_icloud <- function(f, tries = 4) {
  for (i in seq_len(tries)) {
    obj <- tryCatch(readRDS(f), error = function(e) e)
    if (!inherits(obj, "error")) return(obj)
    try(system2("brctl", c("download", shQuote(f)), stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE), silent = TRUE)
    invisible(tryCatch(readBin(f, "raw", file.info(f)$size), error = function(e) NULL))  # fault in
    Sys.sleep(1.5)
  }
  stop("could not read ", f, " after ", tries, " tries (iCloud eviction?).")
}

# Load the slim LOO sidecars for a set of fit numbers into a named list.
load_loo_sidecars <- function(nums, dir = FIT_DIR) {
  out <- list()
  for (num in nums) {
    f <- file.path(dir, sprintf("loo_tps%d.rds", num))
    if (file.exists(f)) out[[paste0("fit_tps", num)]] <- read_rds_icloud(f)
  }
  out
}
```


###################################
Model definition table + runner.
`fit_defs` lists the fixed-effects part of each model (fit 1..10), transcribed from the original
hand-written chunks. The base model appended to each is:
  n_l_75 ~ <fixef> + s(water_year_day) + offset(log(Volume))
########################################
```{r}
# Fixed-effects part of each model ("" = null model: smooth + offset + intercept only).
fit_defs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~num, ~fixef,
  1L,   "",
  2L,   "out30_z",
  3L,   "out30_z + distance_along_channel_z",
  4L,   "out30_z + distance_m_z",
  5L,   "out30_z + distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z",
  6L,   "out30_z * distance_along_channel_z",
  7L,   "out30_z * distance_m_z",
  8L,   "out30_z * distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z",
  9L,   "out30_z * distance_m_z + distance_along_channel_z",
  10L,  "out30_z * (distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z)"
)

# Build the full brms formula for a given fixed-effects string.
build_tps_formula <- function(fixef) {
  rhs <- c(fixef, "s(water_year_day)", "offset(log(Volume))")
  rhs <- rhs[nzchar(trimws(rhs))]          # drop empty fixef (null model)
  as.formula(paste("n_l_75 ~", paste(rhs, collapse = " + ")))
}

# Fit ONE model, compute moment-matched LOO, save the full fit + a lightweight LOO sidecar
# (the part needed for ELPD ranking / stacking weights), append the summary, free memory.
# save_pars(all = TRUE): unlike the k-fold notebooks, moment matching needs the auxiliary draws.
fit_tps_model <- function(num, fixef,
                          data    = tow_12_6_tps_nona,
                          priors  = catch_priors,
                          iter    = 3000,
                          warmup  = 2000,
                          chains  = 4,
                          control = list(max_treedepth = 12, adapt_delta = 0.99),
                          dir     = FIT_DIR,
                          out_txt = OUT_TXT) {
  form <- build_tps_formula(fixef)
  message("=== Fitting fit_tps", num, " ===")
  print(form)

  fit <- brm(
    formula = form,
    family  = negbinomial(link = "log"),
    data    = data,
    prior   = priors,
    iter    = iter, warmup = warmup, chains = chains,
    control = control,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
  )

  fit <- add_loo_mm(fit)

  # Full fit (posterior draws -> conditional effects / CIs / forest plots)
  saveRDS(fit, file = file.path(dir, sprintf("fit_tps%d.rds", num)))
  # Lightweight LOO criterion (ELPD -> ranking / stacking weights) without loading the big fit.
  # Slimmed (psis_object dropped) -> ~60 KB, so it is not evicted by iCloud like the big fits.
  saveRDS(slim_loo(fit$criteria$loo), file = file.path(dir, sprintf("loo_tps%d.rds", num)))

  # Append the summary to the shared printout file (same file as before).
  fileConn <- file(out_txt, open = "a")
  cat(sprintf("\n\n\nSummary of fit_tps%d:\n\n", num), file = fileConn)
  cat(capture.output(summary(fit)), file = fileConn, sep = "\n")
  close(fileConn)

  rm(fit); gc()
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Loop over a set of fit numbers (default: all 10).
run_tps_fits <- function(nums = fit_defs$num, defs = fit_defs, ...) {
  unknown <- setdiff(nums, defs$num)
  if (length(unknown)) {
    stop("No fixed-effects definition for fit number(s): ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
  }
  for (num in nums) {
    fixef <- defs$fixef[match(num, defs$num)]
    fit_tps_model(num = num, fixef = fixef, ...)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```


###################################
Run the fits.
Each fit + moment-matched LOO is slow; run this interactively, not on knit.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
# Run all 10 (or pass a subset, e.g. run_tps_fits(c(1, 5, 10))).
run_tps_fits(nums = 1:10)
```


###################################
Reload LOO results and rank models by ELPD.
Reads the lightweight LOO sidecars (fast — no need to load the full fits), runs loo_compare,
and writes the ranking. Re-run any time after more fits finish.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
fit_nums <- 1:10

loo_results <- load_loo_sidecars(fit_nums)

if (length(loo_results) < 2) {
  stop("Need at least two fits with LOO results to compare; run the fits first.")
}

# ELPD comparison ranking (best model on top, elpd_diff relative to it)
loo_comparisons_catch_tps <- loo_compare(loo_results)
print(loo_comparisons_catch_tps)

write.csv(
  as.data.frame(loo_comparisons_catch_tps),
  file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit_tps_landscape1-10_catch_loo_comparisons.csv")
)
```


###################################
Model stacking weights.
Stacking weights (Yao et al. 2018) from the same moment-matched LOO objects — for model-averaged
predictions / ensemble graphing. Saved as a sidecar so the ensemble code never reloads the fits.
########################################
```{r eval=FALSE}
fit_nums <- 1:10

loo_results <- load_loo_sidecars(fit_nums)

# Stacking weights (default LOO-based optimal predictive stacking)
stacking_weights_tps <- loo_model_weights(loo_results, method = "stacking")
print(stacking_weights_tps)
saveRDS(stacking_weights_tps, file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit_tps_landscape1-10_catch_stacking_weights.rds"))

# Optional: pseudo-BMA+ weights for comparison

```
